# @eltonbautista/vue

Cabinet is a small, playful Vue 3 component library with an arcade-cabinet feel and a tested accessibility contract on every component.

**Components:** `CabButton`, `CabTextField`, `CabCheckbox`, `CabSwitch`, `CabSelect`, `CabTabs`, `CabDialog`, `CabCard`.

## Install

```sh
npm i @eltonbautista/vue @eltonbautista/tokens
```

```ts
// main.ts
import '@eltonbautista/tokens/tokens.css'   // design tokens (CSS custom properties)
import '@eltonbautista/tokens/fonts.css'    // Sora + Outfit (optional)
import '@eltonbautista/vue/style.css'       // component styles
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CabButton, CabTextField } from '@eltonbautista/vue'
const email = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <CabTextField v-model="email" label="Email" type="email" />
  <CabButton>Book a seat</CabButton>
</template>
```

## Accessibility

Every component follows a WAI-ARIA APG pattern and documents its keyboard map, focus behaviour and screen-reader output. Each one is tested in a real browser for keyboard interaction and axe violations. See the Storybook docs for each component's Accessibility section.

content.text:
The landing page is in `src/App.vue`, and `npm run build` succeeds with no errors. I haven't opened it in a browser or run any accessibility checks, so the WCAG 2.2 AA and keyboard behaviour are untested.

- **Title and intro:** an `h1` ("Game Design Weekend") with a short intro. The title and intro wording is my own placeholder, so replace it with your real copy.
- **Tracks:** three `CabCard`s, each linking to `/tracks/board`, `/tracks/digital` or `/tracks/larp`. The card's title is the link and its hit area covers the whole card, so clicking anywhere on it navigates. For keyboard users that gives one tab stop per card.
- **Sign-up form:**
  - **Fields:** name, email and experience level.
  - **Validation:** native browser validation is off. On submit, any problems show as error messages, and focus moves to the first invalid field.
  - **Code of conduct:** the submit button stays enabled, and the form only proceeds once the code-of-conduct checkbox is ticked. If it isn't ticked you get an error message.
- **Email reminders:** a `CabSwitch` that applies the change the moment it's toggled, with no save button. Each change is announced to screen readers ("Email reminders turned on/off"). Nothing is actually saved anywhere yet, since there's no backend, so it only updates local state.
- **Confirmation:** a valid submit opens a `CabDialog` showing the name, email and level, with "Go back" and "Confirm booking" buttons. Confirming closes it and shows a thank-you message announced to screen readers. Nothing is sent to a server either, so the booking isn't stored anywhere.

The checkbox component has no error prop, so I show its error as separate text. That text isn't programmatically tied to the checkbox, so a screen reader announces it as an alert but doesn't link it to the field.
